verses.verse:
वाद्यम् विहाय फूत्कारम् पावकादौ न्यसेत्पुरा।
तत्र सिध्दम् हि फूत्कारम् वाद्ये सभ्यक् प्रसाधयेत्।७२।
verses.text: Leaving the instrument aside, one should first direct the breath at fire and the like; then the breath perfected there should be properly applied to the instrument.

commentary.text: That is, a new practitioner should first practise blowing at a fire; when the practice of blowing at a fire has been mastered over a week, then one should try for sound in the bānsurī with that breath. For when the lips are not balanced, the flow of the breath becomes crooked, and when too much air comes out in the breath, the breath does not last. So, to make the stream of the breath long, thin and straight, it will be right, on spiritual, scientific and Vedic evidence, to regard Agni deva (the god of fire) himself as the very first guru (teacher). Śrī Manu, the author of the dharmaśāstra, has also given fire the place of guru: (gururagnirdvijātīnām) [fire is the guru of the twice-born]; (tamaso mā jyotirgamaya) [lead me from darkness to light]. All these sayings create faith in fire in us, and through faith both skill and knowledge become easy to gain. In this way, by trying many times, the breath is mastered and begins to produce a beautiful sound in the bānsurī in a balanced way. If the flow of the breath is joined to the mukharandhra (mouth-hole) on the bānsurī, there can be three kinds of it, of which only the third kind is correct; the other two kinds are incorrect.
